title: Business Line Manager - Money Flows
description: About Ledger We’re a team of experts pushing the limits of what’s possible, united by our common goal to unlock true freedom through digital ownership, making technology accessible for all. We believe in a world where users, creators and enterprises manage their value with ownership and freedom. Our curiosity drives us to innovate, empowering individuals on a global scale. We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger. At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries. The team: With over 8 million signers sold worldwide, Ledger Wallet is where Ledger users manage and grow their assets. Transactional Services (buy, sell, swap, trading and stablecoin products) is its main source of service revenue. Money Flows connects users' crypto to the fiat world in both directions: on/off-ramp , cash-to-stablecoin , Card , and the growing P2P and Payments use cases. Users buy crypto with fiat or sell it back to their bank, move cash into stablecoins, and spend crypto with a card, all through specialist partners. It is the entry and exit door of the Ledger Wallet economy and a key lever to diversify Transactional Services revenue. The role reports to the Senior Director, Transactional Services. What you’ll be doing: You own and grow Money Flows end to end - revenue, economics, partner ecosystem and the quality of every fiat journey in Ledger Wallet - with a General Manager mindset over a business run mostly through external partners and cross-functional teams. The ambition is to grow revenue 10x in two to three years, through a strategy and roadmap you define and turn into quantified milestones. Key responsibilities include: Business Line Ownership & Revenue Delivery: Being ultimately accountable for Money Flows revenue, volume and take rate across buy, sell, cash-to-stablecoin, Card, P2P and Payments. Building and defending the forecast, querying the data yourself, and separating market effects from the levers the team controls. Monetization & Pricing: Owning take rate by line, partner and payment method. Turning volume into direct or indirect revenue (zero-fee partners, cash-to-stablecoin flows), and keeping pricing/product competitive against exchanges, neobanks and other wallets. Partner Management & Business Development: Identifying, signing, managing and negotiating with the ramp, payment, stablecoin and card-issuing partner bench - on pricing, geographic and payment-method coverage, conversion, KYC friction and operational quality. Managing concentration risk, onboarding new providers to close gaps, and running a monthly review with each partner. Card Programme Ownership: Running the card programme: economics, activation and dormancy, issuer and processor performance, card-scheme negotiations (including geo expansion), and the go-to-market with Marketing. Ledger Wallet Experience: Working with the Product Line Manager to improve the Buy, Sell, Card and Pay journeys, and making sure every release ships with a coordinated go-to-market. Stablecoin & Payments Roadmap: Shaping how Ledger captures stablecoin and payment use cases - cash-to-stablecoin, Pay and peer-to-peer flows - together with Product, within local regulatory frameworks (MiCA,...) with Legal and Compliance, informed by close tracking of the ramp, stablecoin and card landscape. Operational Excellence & Observability: Partner SLAs, incident management and fast action to protect users, Ledger and revenue; conversion, failed-payment and KYC-drop monitoring; and closing measurement gaps so every line can be steered on data. Cross-Functional Delivery: Driving execution across Product, Technology, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Pricing, Marketing/CRM and other business lines - all of it outside your reporting lines - to ship improvements, drive growth and resolve issues. What we’re looking for: Ownership mindset: A demonstrated ability to own a business line or revenue stream end to end and make data-driven decisions. You are energized by being accountable for a P&L line and delivering the budget, including in a soft market. Exceptional quantitative skills: A strong track record of using data to drive decisions and manage execution. You enjoy digging into the numbers yourself and separating market effect from execution. Commercial & business development experience: Proven results negotiating and managing external partners on pricing, terms and performance. You like using data and leverage to improve terms, coverage and quality, and building relationships that compound over time. Sales / business development experience is highly valued. Payments industry experience (required): Experience in payments (for example at Visa, Adyen, Stripe or dLocal), with hands-on knowledge of payments and acquiring - conversion funnels, KYC, fraud and chargeback dynamics. Card ecosystem: Experience in the card ecosystem - issuing, processing, card schemes or programme management, including interchange and programme economics - is a strong plus. Operational excellence: Evidence of running something with rigor - managing operational risk, reducing errors and optimizing conversion or engagement. You are comfortable running live lines while shaping new ones, such as stablecoins, payments and card programs. Influence in a matrixed organization: The proven ability to align Product, Tech, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Marketing behind your priorities and drive cross-functional initiatives without direct authority. Consumer fintech / service-revenue background: Experience in a high-volume transactional or service-revenue business is highly desirable; a B2C background is a strong plus. Fintech or equivalent service experience is a must. Digital assets: Interest in stablecoins and crypto is desirable, as the crypto knowledge needed can be learned faster than payments expertise. Familiarity with MiCA and European payments regulation is a plus. AI: Strong appetite for what AI can bring to analysis and operations is a must. Total English fluency. The role is based in Paris; French is not a prerequisite for social or work life in our office. At Ledger, we are dedicated to continually investing in our employees which is why we offer more than just salaries; we provide comprehensive compensation packages that include a wide range of benefits. Here are some of the benefits you can look forward to: Flexible work options - Our hybrid policy allows employees to work from home up to 3 times per week Health & Wellness support - Health and Life Insurance. Financial growth opportunities - Employees can become shareholders in Ledger as well as other financial benefits depending on your country of work. Commuter allowance - Ledger offers a commuter allowance to contribute to your preferred means of transportation. Learning & Development - A comprehensive suite of training solutions providing a personalised learning experience for every employee. For regionally specific benefits, your Talent Acquisition contact will be able to provide you with more information. We’re committed to building an inclusive hiring process. If you need any adjustments or accommodations, just let us know, we’ll do our best to support you. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

Chez Centreon, la fiabilité est notre métier : nos clients nous confient la supervision de leurs infrastructures critiques. Nos propres services doivent donc être irréprochables. Au sein de l’équipe SRE, vous êtes garant·e de la disponibilité, de la performance et de la résilience des plateformes qui portent nos trois produits, sur AWS et sur Outscale, notre cloud souverain.

En tant qu’ingénieur·e SRE senior, vous portez des projets structurants de bout en bout et vous entraînez l’équipe avec vous. Dans une petite équipe où chacun touche à beaucoup de sujets, nous recherchons un profil polyvalent plutôt qu’un expert d’un seul outil.

Missions

  • Garantir la disponibilité et la performance de nos plateformes, et anticiper les problèmes avant qu’ils ne touchent nos clients

  • Participer à la gestion des incidents, aux post-mortems et à l’astreinte, organisée en rotation dans l’équipe

  • Faire évoluer nos plateformes Kubernetes, futur cœur de notre architecture, et automatiser l’infrastructure en Infrastructure as Code

  • Industrialiser les déploiements et accompagner les équipes de développement vers le déploiement en autonomie, en incarnant les bonnes pratiques SRE

  • Contribuer à la sécurité et à la conformité : correctifs, protection des points d’entrée, gestion des secrets

  • Industrialiser l’usage de l’IA dans nos pratiques, avec des agents qui aident à diagnostiquer les incidents et automatisent les opérations courantes

  • Assurer la veille technologique et contribuer à l’optimisation des coûts

  • Former les nouveaux arrivants et représenter Centreon lors d’événements et auprès de la communauté

Exemples de projets : Selon les priorités de l’équipe

  • Migrer une plateforme de supervision vers Kubernetes

  • Industrialiser la reprise après sinistre, avec des exercices réguliers et prouvés

  • Etendre nos produits sur le cloud souverain

  • Généraliser OpenTelemetry sur nos services et nos infrastructures

  • Automatiser le diagnostic d’incidents avec des agents IA

Stack technique

  • Cloud et conteneurs : AWS, Outscale, Kubernetes (EKS, OKS), Helm

  • Automatisation et CI/CD : Terraform, Terrakube, Ansible, Packer, GitHub Actions, Argo CD, Argo Workflows

  • Observabilité et sécurité : OpenTelemetry, CloudWatch, stack d’observabilité open source, Vault

  • Développement et IA : Go, Python, Bash, Claude Code


Profil et compétences

  • Vous avez au moins 5 ans d’expérience en SRE, DevOps ou exploitation d’infrastructures cloud, sur des environnements de production critiques

  • Vous avez mené des projets d’infrastructure d’envergure portés de bout en bout (migration, conteneurisation, reprise après sinistre)

  • Vous avez une solide maîtrise de Linux, des fondamentaux réseau et de Kubernetes en production

  • Vous avez une pratique avancée de l’Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) et d’un cloud public, idéalement AWS

  • Vous maitrisez l’exploitation de bases de données (MySQL/PostgreSQL) et de stockage réseau

  • Vous avez une culture de l’observabilité et de la gestion d’incidents (post-mortems, SLO/SLI)

  • Vous avez la capacité à développer de l’outillage en Go, Python ou Bash

  • Vous avez l’esprit de partage et vous êtes pédagogue

  • Vous parlez l’anglais

Les plus qui feront la différence

  • Vous avez une expérience d’un cloud souverain

  • Vous connaissez le monde de la supervision IT et de l’open source

  • L’IA n’a plus de secret pour vous, vous l’utilisez au service de l’exploitation

Ce que nous offrons

  • Un rôle au cœur de la qualité de service d’un éditeur qui fait de la fiabilité son métier

  • Une vraie influence sur l’architecture, la sécurité et la stratégie cloud

  • Une culture d’automatisation et d’amélioration continue

  • Société en forte croissance (+20%  en 2025) dans un environnement international

  • Venez apprécier nos locaux avec terrasse à Olympiade - Métro ligne 14 (immeubles accessibles PMR) ou à Toulouse - Métro ligne B à  Compans Caffarelli  

  • Remote friendly : 2 jours de télétravail par semaine possible

  • RTT et Carte Tickets restaurant

  • Events réguliers

  • Un programme d'Onboarding

  • Pleins d'autres avantages --> https://centreon.recruitee.com/qui-sommes-nous


Nous avons à cœur de mettre en avant la diversité au sein de notre entreprise. Tous les candidats qualifiés seront pris en considération pour un emploi sans distinction de race, de couleur, de religion, de sexe, d'orientation sexuelle, d'identité de genre, de nationalité ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la loi dans le pays où le candidat postule.

Ce poste est ouvert aux personnes en situation de handicap.

Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data. About Us Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing. Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo. The Role You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work. Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked. We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging. What You'll Do Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them. Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads. Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first. Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own. Put AI to work on adoption: decide which steps an agent should do for the user, ship them with the team, and measure whether people keep using them. Work with Growth on launches and product marketing, and with our customer engineers on whatever is blocking rollouts at customers. Part of it is showing us something you shipped that you'd still be proud to demo. Second interview (60 min): a working session on a real Soda adoption problem Culture fit (45 min) We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly. Requirements You Should Have 5+ years in product, including at least 2 owning growth, activation, onboarding, or adoption in B2B SaaS : you were accountable for a metric for long enough to see whether your changes worked. In your application, tell us which metric it was, where it started and where it ended, what you shipped, and what didn't work. Product craft and taste : you love software and have used a lot of it yourself, so you know what a good product feels like. You keep scope small, work in short cycles with engineers and designers, run your own customer calls, and have well-reasoned opinions about UX. An AI-native way of working and building : you've shipped an AI-powered feature and measured whether people use it, you prototype with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.), and you're happy to open a small PR yourself for something like a copy change. You do your own analysis : you write SQL, build funnels yourself, and know when a sample is too small to conclude anything. Experience with technical products : you've built for engineers or data teams and are comfortable talking about pipelines, warehouses, and APIs. Clear writing and comfort working async : we're a distributed team across 12+ countries, and most decisions happen in writing, in English. The five years don't all have to be in a PM role. If you were a product engineer or a founder and owned a growth metric, please apply. Good to Have Data quality, data observability, data governance, or data infrastructure experience. Experience with product-led growth at a company that also sells to enterprises. Experience with Shape Up or another fixed-time, variable-scope way of working. Benefits What We Offer Compensation €120,000–140,000/year + equity. Outside Belgium, this is a contractor position. Fully remote (EU-based), with a Belgian office available if you want one. In-person kickoffs every two months in cool locations across Europe, three days with the whole product and engineering team. All the tokens you need, across all frontier models. Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement. A senior team that ships, across 12+ countries. Our Values We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful product and roadmap decisions. ❤️ Why you will love to join Soda You own the adoption metrics : you decide how we measure adoption and what we do to improve it. Lots of room to improve : we already have enterprise customers and usage data, and we've done very little growth work so far. Your own engineering team : you'll work with dedicated engineers who build agentically, so your ideas get shipped quickly. Be part of a transformation : data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it. Work on your own terms : fully remote, flexible hours, colleagues in 12+ countries. 😡 What you might not love Rapidly changing priorities : our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done. Small numbers : we have relatively few accounts and feedback is slow. If you're used to deciding from consumer-scale data, you may find that frustrating. No playbook : this is the first dedicated growth PM role at Soda. raw.title: Senior Growth Product Manager
raw.description:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.

Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data.

About Us

Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing.

Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo.

The Role

You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work.

Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked.

We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging.

What You'll Do

  • Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them.
  • Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads.
  • Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first.
  • Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own.
  • Put AI to work on adoption: decide which steps an agent should do for the user, ship them with the team, and measure whether people keep using them.
  • Work with Growth on launches and product marketing, and with our customer engineers on whatever is blocking rollouts at customers.

Hiring Process

  1. Application: your CV, plus a short answer about one metric you moved (what it was, what you shipped, what happened, and what didn't work)
  2. 15-minute phone screen
  3. First interview (60 min): a deep dive into product growth work you've done. Part of it is showing us something you shipped that you'd still be proud to demo.
  4. Second interview (60 min): a working session on a real Soda adoption problem
  5. Culture fit (45 min)

We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.

Requirements

You Should Have

  • 5+ years in product, including at least 2 owning growth, activation, onboarding, or adoption in B2B SaaS: you were accountable for a metric for long enough to see whether your changes worked. In your application, tell us which metric it was, where it started and where it ended, what you shipped, and what didn't work.
  • Product craft and taste: you love software and have used a lot of it yourself, so you know what a good product feels like. You keep scope small, work in short cycles with engineers and designers, run your own customer calls, and have well-reasoned opinions about UX.
  • An AI-native way of working and building: you've shipped an AI-powered feature and measured whether people use it, you prototype with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.), and you're happy to open a small PR yourself for something like a copy change.
  • You do your own analysis: you write SQL, build funnels yourself, and know when a sample is too small to conclude anything.
  • Experience with technical products: you've built for engineers or data teams and are comfortable talking about pipelines, warehouses, and APIs.
  • Clear writing and comfort working async: we're a distributed team across 12+ countries, and most decisions happen in writing, in English.

The five years don't all have to be in a PM role. If you were a product engineer or a founder and owned a growth metric, please apply.

Good to Have

  • Data quality, data observability, data governance, or data infrastructure experience.
  • Experience with product-led growth at a company that also sells to enterprises.
  • Experience with Shape Up or another fixed-time, variable-scope way of working.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Compensation €120,000–140,000/year + equity.
  • Outside Belgium, this is a contractor position.
  • Fully remote (EU-based), with a Belgian office available if you want one.
  • In-person kickoffs every two months in cool locations across Europe, three days with the whole product and engineering team.
  • All the tokens you need, across all frontier models.
  • Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement.
  • A senior team that ships, across 12+ countries.

Our Values

We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful product and roadmap decisions.

❤️ Why you will love to join Soda

  • You own the adoption metrics: you decide how we measure adoption and what we do to improve it.
  • Lots of room to improve: we already have enterprise customers and usage data, and we've done very little growth work so far.
  • Your own engineering team: you'll work with dedicated engineers who build agentically, so your ideas get shipped quickly.
  • Be part of a transformation: data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it.
  • Work on your own terms: fully remote, flexible hours, colleagues in 12+ countries.

😡 What you might not love

  • Rapidly changing priorities: our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done.
  • Small numbers: we have relatively few accounts and feedback is slow. If you're used to deciding from consumer-scale data, you may find that frustrating.
  • No playbook: this is the first dedicated growth PM role at Soda.

Publisher integrations

raw.description:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

About the Role
We are building next-generation interceptor drones and are looking for a Senior Jet Engine Design Engineer to lead the development of small-scale jet propulsion systems (12–25 kg thrust class), from concept to flight-ready hardware. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role in a fast-moving startup environment where speed and iteration matter more than lengthy upfront studies.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop new small jet engines (12–25 kg thrust range) in-house, optimized for very low production cost

  • Own the aerodynamic design of turbine components, balancing performance, manufacturability, and cost

  • Design a large portion of the turbine for metal 3D printing (additive manufacturing), leveraging design-for-AM principles to reduce part count, weight, and cost

  • Work closely with 3D printing operations to define printable geometries, tolerances, post-processing, and qualify parts for flight use

  • Drive a rapid, fail-fast iteration process: build, test, learn, and redesign quickly rather than relying on long analytical phases before prototyping

  • Integrate propulsion systems into airframes such as flying wings and other interceptor drone configurations, working with aerostructures and systems teams

  • Apply and enforce design rules for operation in extreme environments (cold and hot climates, rain, humidity, icing conditions) to ensure engine reliability across the full operational envelope

  • Contribute to engine testing (bench and flight), performance validation, and continuous design improvement

Candidate Profile:

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in jet engine / gas turbine design, with a proven track record of having designed and delivered engine models (not just component-level work)

  • Strong hands-on experience with small jet engines in the 12–25 kg thrust class

  • Solid global understanding of jet engine architecture: compressor, combustor, turbine, fuel system, controls, and their interactions

  • Experience designing turbine/engine components for metal additive manufacturing (DfAM), and practical knowledge of metal 3D printing processes and constraints

  • Comfortable working in a rapid-iteration, fail-fast development culture rather than a traditional long-cycle aerospace process

  • Experience integrating propulsion systems into airframes (flying wing or similar unconventional platforms is a strong plus)

  • Knowledge of design requirements for extreme operating environments (temperature extremes, precipitation, icing)

  • Ability to work autonomously in a small, fast-paced startup team, wearing multiple hats when needed

Nice to Have

  • Experience with UAV/drone propulsion specifically (vs. manned aviation)

  • Familiarity with low-cost manufacturing strategies for defense/dual-use hardware

  • Prior startup or skunkworks experience

raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

Mistral AI is looking for AI Scientists with deep machine learning expertise and hands-on engineering experience to expand what Mistral's agentic tools can do across the engineering lifecycle across CAE (CFD, FEA etc) and EDA/Semi..

Within AI4Engineering Science, your core work is building the pre and post-training data for Mistral's LLMs to reason about and execute real engineering tasks. Alongside this, you'll help shape the agent architectures and harness that let these models operate reliably inside multi-step engineering workflows, not just answer isolated questions.

You'll work closely with domain experts across CAE and EDA to ground this work in how engineers actually work, and with the broader research team to translate that domain grounding into training signal and evaluation benchmarks that measure genuine task competence.

What You Will Do

  • Design pretraining, SFT, and RL data for engineering tasks across CAD, CAE, and semiconductor/EDA

  • Define verifiers and evaluation criteria that capture what "correct" and "high-quality" actually mean for each engineering task, beyond surface-level plausibility

  • Design and improve agent architectures and harnesses: how models plan, call tools, recover from errors, and chain steps together across long-horizon engineering workflows

  • Build evaluation benchmarks and diagnostic tooling to identify where models fail on engineering tasks, and trace those failures back to gaps in data, reward design, or agent scaffolding

  • Collaborate with domain experts across CAEand EDA (and the science and solutions teams more broadly) to identify which engineering workflows are highest-value to target next

  • Contribute to Mistral's broader pre and post-training research, sharing findings and methodology across the science organization

What We're Looking For

  • Fluent English with excellent communication skills, able to explain technical ML and engineering concepts to both engineering and non-technical audiences

  • Deep, hands-on machine learning expertise, particularly LLM development

  • Demonstrated experience running, debugging, and validating real engineering workflows in at least one of CAD, CAE, semiconductor simulation, or EDA.

  • You write clean, readable Python code and are comfortable in Linux/HPC environments

  • Self-directed, you don't need detailed roadmaps to make progress

  • Low-ego, collaborative, and eager to learn at the intersection of engineering and ML

It would be great if you

  • Have experience building or fine-tuning agentic systems (tool use, multi-step planning, agent orchestration frameworks)

  • Have experience with reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF/RLVR, or preference-based training

  • Have industrial or academic experience with CAE, or EDA tools (e.g. SolidWorks, CATIA, Fluent, Abaqus, LS-DYNA, STAR-CCM+, Cadence/Synopsys/Siemens EDA tools)

  • Have contributed to a large open-source or industry codebase

  • Have publications in engineering and ML venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, JFM, AIAA, etc.)

 

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

raw.title: Director, Customer Success
raw.description:
About Prudentia Sciences

Prudentia Sciences is the scientific intelligence layer powering life sciences dealmaking. We bring together expert-developed scientific diligence frameworks, AI reasoning trained on drug development, and a unified evidence base to accelerate investment in breakthrough therapies. As a trusted third party operating between buyer and seller, we help build conviction through every stage of the deal, faster. We replace fragmented workflows with a single system that surfaces what matters earlier.

 

Backed by GV (Google Ventures), McKesson, Iaso Ventures, Virtue, and SignalFire - and built by people who have sat on every side of the table in life sciences dealmaking - we're on a mission to bring expert scientific judgment to every deal decision, at AI scale.

 

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Director of Customer Success to manage and scale a portfolio of strategic biopharma accounts. You'll own commercial outcomes for Top 25 biopharma customers, driving platform adoption, retention, and expansion to build a “business within the business”. Customer feedback from your portfolio will directly inform our product roadmap and operating model. You’ll operate with the judgment of an owner, not just execute a playbook.

What You'll Own

Commercial strategy

  • Own a portfolio of strategic biopharma accounts; drive the full commercial lifecycle - from implementation and onboarding through to retention and partnership expansion

  • Develop and execute account-level strategy, identifying expansion opportunities and leading renewal negotiations to achieve industry-leading retention rates

  • Monitor usage patterns, engagement signals, and business outcomes to proactively grow accounts and manage partnership signals

  • Transform satisfied customers into vocal advocates who provide references, case studies, testimonials, and speak at industry events

  • Serve as the voice of the customer to Product, Engineering, Sales, and Scientific teams, ensuring market feedback drives our product roadmap and strategic priorities

Lead Implementation and Drive Adoption

  • Orchestrate complex customer implementations including platform configuration, custom development, and data integrations aligned to customer use cases

  • Design and execute account-specific onboarding strategies, facilitating executive workshops, design sessions, and hands-on trainings that accelerate time-to-value

  • Proactively communicate product updates, new capabilities, and innovative use cases to maximize customer value realization

Provide Expert Technical Support

  • Diagnose and resolve platform issues through systematic troubleshooting, documenting problems clearly and coordinating with Engineering on appropriate resolution paths

  • Develop deep platform expertise that enables you to answer complex technical questions and guide customers through sophisticated workflows

  • Create feedback loops that ensure technical issues inform long-term product improvements

Who You Are

Essential Qualifications

  • 8+ years of customer success, management consulting, partnerships, account management, or implementation experience in pharmaceutical, biopharma, biotech, or life sciences industries

  • Working knowledge of drug development processes, portfolio management, and deal evaluation frameworks

  • Demonstrated ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder decision-making within large enterprise organizations

  • Strong technical aptitude, with the ability to quickly master sophisticated software platforms and translate technical capabilities into business value

  • Exceptional executive communication skills

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with comfort operating in fast-paced, high-growth environments where priorities evolve quickly

 

Bonus points

  • Direct experience in biopharma Search & Evaluation, Business Development, Licensing, Portfolio Management, or Strategy roles

  • Track record of driving measurable customer outcomes, achieving retention and expansion targets

  • Hands-on experience with AI/ML platforms, advanced analytics tools, or decision intelligence software

  • Proficiency with customer success platforms (HubSpot, etc.)

  • Advanced degree (MS, PhD, MBA) in life sciences, business, or a related field

Location

We are strongly prioritizing candidates based in London (UK), Dublin (Ireland), or Basel (Switzerland) to support our EU-based clients. Today this role will be remote as we do not have a physical office in these locations, but as we scale, we intend to be hybrid 2x per week (Tues/Thurs).

 
 

Compensation: €89K – €110K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus • Multiple Ranges

  • Dublin, Ireland • €89K – €110K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus
  • London, England • £85K – £110K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus
  • Basel, Switzerland • CHF 117K – CHF 150K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus

title: Science Manager – Nature-based Solutions (80-100%)
description: As a Science Manager in Climeworks Solutions, you make sure that our nature-based solutions (NBS) portfolio meets the same demanding quality bar we apply to all our carbon dioxide removal offerings. Your focus is on Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR), Improved Forest Management (IFM) and Mangroves, but you are not limited to these. You will screen the market, identify and assess priority projects, and carry out due diligence on potential partners. You form and defend Climeworks Solutions' own, independent scientific view on the quality, risks and fit of NBS projects. You keep our assessment criteria up to date and apply them in practice. You work closely with the sourcing team to shape our approach to nature credits, from first supplier contact to partnerships and product positioning. This role gives you real influence on how we build our nature offering and how the wider removal market develops. Quality framework development: You adapt and sharpen Climeworks' quality assessment frameworks for nature-based pathways. You draw on the newest published methodologies and on standards as they evolve. Supplier assessment and monitoring: You build constructive relationships with relevant suppliers. You rate and benchmark their projects. Over time, you track how project quality and delivery change and flag any concerns early. Project due diligence: You run in-depth technical, scientific and commercial reviews of key projects. These cover additionality, measurability, carbon accounting, co-benefits, reversal risk and delivery risk. You combine many data sources, including GIS analysis, project documents and registry information, into clear recommendations. Pathway segmentation: As the CDR industry matures, you group projects into sub-pathways and archetypes. For each one, you develop a well-founded view of what quality means. Market intelligence and prioritization: Together with Sourcing, you map the project landscape across key regions and pathways. You identify the strongest projects and recommend them, based on methodological robustness, pricing, reputation and delivery record. Contracting support: You help Sourcing draft contracts with approved suppliers. You focus on negotiating quality-related terms and amendments. Partnership development: You help build relationships with important players in the ecosystem, such as rating agencies, registries, NGOs and other opinion leaders. Pathway strategy: You work with colleagues in Science, Sourcing and the wider Commercial team to define the strategy for each nature-based pathway. You consider market trends, quality benchmarks, demand and supply. Sales support: You advise on project selection and answer technical questions in customer discussions, pitches and tenders. Knowledge sharing: You keep colleagues informed about scientific progress, new methodologies and market developments in nature-based solutions. Education: You have a Master's degree in a relevant field, such as ecology, conservation science, environmental or natural sciences, forestry or geography. A PhD is an advantage. Experience: You have hands-on experience in nature-based carbon projects. This could be project development, project design documentation, independent project ratings, MRV, carbon modelling or biodiversity research. Experience in carbon markets and CDR, and with standards such as Verra, Gold Standard, Plan Vivo or Isometric, is a strong plus. Analytical skills: You work confidently with large and varied datasets, including GIS and statistical analysis. You are precise and scientifically rigorous, and you can reach sound conclusions even when data is incomplete. Critical thinking: You question assumptions, spot inconsistencies and find practical solutions by connecting findings across projects. Business judgement: You weigh commercial and strategic factors when assessing projects and shaping strategy. Communication and language: You explain complex topics in a clear and credible way, and you can show how robust your assessments are. You are fluent in written and spoken English. Way of working: You take ownership and manage several projects at once, with clean documentation. You are comfortable working across teams and in different environments. You balance independent judgement with close collaboration. Our promise: At Climeworks, you are accepted for who you are, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply – regardless of background, identity, or experience. Studies show that women and individuals from minority backgrounds often only apply for jobs when they meet 100% of the listed criteria. If this sounds like you, don’t hold back. If you think you’d make a great fit for this role, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t check every single box. Let’s tackle one of humankind’s greatest challenges together. What we offer: Time Off: Enjoy 25 paid vacation days every year, plus public holidays. Flexibility: Work how it suits you best. We offer a hybrid work setup and up to 4 weeks of remote work annually within any EU country. Ownership: Fair base pay paired with an equity package – because your contributions matter. Family Support: Inclusive parental leave. Continuous Learning: Dedicated budget to invest in your professional growth. Referral Rewards: Help us grow our team and earn bonuses for your successful referrals. Salary: At Climeworks, salary ranges are assigned to a job based on the level of seniority and the location specific market median of similar jobs according to external benchmark surveys. Individual compensation depends on your skills, experience, and the value you bring to the team. Formalities:   This position is based in Opfikon, Zurich, and we ask that you work onsite at least three days per week. The percentage in the job title means flexibility – choose full-time or part-time based on what works for you. We do not accept candidate profiles through recruitment agencies.   • Du stellst die strukturierte Übergabe in den Betrieb sicher und begleitest den Kunden auch nach der Einführung. Sei es im Ticketing, Releases und in der Zusammenarbeit mit der IT-Betriebsorganisation

Dein Profil

  • Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Leitung komplexer Software- oder Digitalisierungsprojekte, idealerweise bei Banken, Versicherungen oder anderen regulierten Finanzinstituten
  • Du fühlst dich an der Schnittstelle zwischen Business und IT, Produktentwicklung und Delivery im Kundenumfeld sicher

raw.title: IoT Embedded Systems Engineer
raw.description:
• Take ownership of the development of IoT systems, with a focus on embedded software, system architecture, and hardware and firmware integration

  • Design and develop robust, efficient, and scalable embedded software for IoT products based on microcontroller platforms and, optionally, Linux based systems

  • Provide technical guidance for hardware development in collaboration with external partners, including reviewing and challenging PCB designs to ensure functionality, quality, and manufacturability

  • Collaborate closely with mechanical, software, and cloud engineering teams to ensure seamless end to end system integration

  • Define and refine product requirements from initial concept through to mass production in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders

  • Develop and integrate prototypes and support the transition from development into serial production together with manufacturing partners

  • Contribute to the continuous evolution of the embedded platform, including MCU based solutions as well as optional Linux and Yocto based components

  • Develop pragmatic testing strategies to ensure the functionality, reliability, and quality of both hardware and firmware

  • Support development and manufacturing partners with debugging, technical documentation, and production ramp up

  • Provide Level 3 technical support for complex system, firmware, and hardware related issues

  • Travel approximately 5 to 10 percent to support development partners, product validation activities, and product launches


  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience

  • Several years of hands on experience in embedded development, including firmware development and hardware related engineering

  • Strong understanding of hardware design and PCB layouts, with the ability to review design decisions and collaborate effectively with hardware development teams

  • Strong expertise in embedded firmware development and software architecture for microcontroller platforms such as ARM Cortex, ESP32, or STM32

  • Experience with sensor integration and wireless communication technologies such as BLE and WiFi

  • Experience with embedded Linux systems, particularly Yocto, is an advantage, especially in environments combining System on Modules with MCU based architectures

  • Broad system level understanding of mechanics, sensors, actuators, and their integration into robust IoT products

  • Hands on experience with hardware testing, debugging tools, and automated production testing

  • Familiarity with certification standards such as CE and FCC is an advantage

  • Fluent in German and English, with additional languages considered a plus

title: Senior Business Analyst / System Engineer CCS – Europäische Standardisierung EU-Rail (50%)
description: Im Rahmen des europäischen Projekts «Europäische Standardisierung CCS-Strecke» arbeiten gemeinsam mit führenden internationalen Bahnindustrieunternehmen wie Siemens, Hitachi, Alstom und CAF sowie europäischen Infrastrukturbetreibern wie DB, SNCF, RFI, ÖBB, Network Rail und ProRail an der Weiterentwicklung und Harmonisierung zukünftiger Bahnsysteme. Das Projekt ist Teil des Europe’s Rail Joint Undertaking (ERJU) und umfasst den System Pillar sowie den Innovation Pillar. Ziel ist die Entwicklung europaweit einheitlicher Betriebsprozesse, Systemarchitekturen und technischer Spezifikationen für die zukünftigen ERTMS-Zielsysteme, insbesondere ETCS Level 2 und Automatic Train Operation (ATO GoA 1/2). Die erarbeiteten Standards bilden die Grundlage für zukünftige europäische Betriebsvorschriften sowie für die Weiterentwicklung und Beschaffung von Sicherungsanlagen. Zur Unterstützung der internationalen Projektarbeiten suchen wir eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit als Senior Business Analyst / System Engineer im Bereich Control, Command and Signalling (CCS). System Engineering: Erarbeitung und Weiterentwicklung von Systemdefinitionen, Systemarchitekturen und technischen Systemspezifikationen im sicherheitsrelevanten Bahnumfeld (CCS). Spezifikationserstellung: Entwicklung und Abstimmung von System- und Schnittstellenspezifikationen unter Berücksichtigung der Gesamtarchitektur sowie zukünftiger Bahnprozesse. Prozesskoordination: Verantwortung für die effiziente Umsetzung und kontinuierliche Optimierung der Arbeitsprozesse (Workstations) zur Erstellung der Systemspezifikationen. Operative Projektunterstützung: Unterstützung bei der Organisation, Koordination und Umsetzung der internationalen Arbeitsorganisation. Qualitätssicherung: Sicherstellung einer konsistenten, vollständigen und qualitativ hochwertigen Integration der Arbeitsergebnisse in die übergeordneten Systemspezifikationen. Stakeholder-Management: Zusammenarbeit und Abstimmung mit internationalen Industriepartnern, europäischen Infrastrukturbetreibern sowie internen und externen Fachspezialisten. Standardisierung: Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung europäisch harmonisierter Betriebsprozesse und technischer Standards für zukünftige ERTMS-Systeme. Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (ETH, Universität oder Fachhochschule) in Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften oder einem verwandten naturwissenschaftlichen Fachgebiet. Umfassende Kenntnisse des Bahnsystems, insbesondere des Bahnbetriebs und der Zugsteuerung. Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Bereich internationale Standardisierung im Bahnumfeld. Fundierte Erfahrung in der Erstellung von System- und Schnittstellenspezifikationen im europäischen Umfeld. Erfahrung mit Application Lifecycle Management Tools, insbesondere Polarion. Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit sowie die Fähigkeit, komplexe technische Inhalte verständlich und zielgruppengerecht zu vermitteln. Sicheres Auftreten im Umgang mit unterschiedlichen nationalen und internationalen Stakeholdern. Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. title: Senior Full Stack Developer TypeScript (Vue / NestJS) (w/m/d) 80-100%
description: Jobbeschreibung Mach mit uns Schweizer Kleinunternehmen noch erfolgreicher! Klingt nach einer grossen Vision? Genau das treibt uns jeden Tag an. Wir bei bexio leben die Philosophie, dass erstklassige, effiziente und smarte Softwarelösungen für jedes KMU zugänglich und erschwinglich sein müssen. Mit dieser Mission sind wir heute die führende Anbieterin für webbasierte Business-Software in der Schweiz. Unser Expansionskurs geht steil nach oben: Über 100'000 zufriedene Kunden, mehr als 7'000 Treuhand-Partner und ein starkes Team von über 150 motivierten Mitarbeitenden sprechen für sich. Um diese Erfolgsgeschichte weiterzuschreiben, suchen wir tatkräftige Unterstützung. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel! Stellenanforderungen Was du bei uns bewegst Als Senior Developer übernimmst du die technische Verantwortung für unseren TypeScript-Stack, mit Vue.js im Frontend und Node.js/NestJS im Backend und gestaltest die Weiterentwicklung von Kontera massgeblich mit. Du konzipierst, implementierst, testest und wartest Produkt-Features End-to-End: von der Benutzeroberfläche über die APIs bis hin zur Datenbank. Du triffst fundierte technische Entscheidungen, um skalierbare und wartbare Software zu entwickeln unter anderem für KI-gestützte Verarbeitungen und asynchrone Workflows. Du erweiterst unsere Integrationen mit Drittsystemen wie Banken, Zahlungsdienstleistern und Buchhaltungslösungen (einschliesslich bexio). Du arbeitest eng mit dem Produktmanagement sowie anderen Teams zusammen und vermittelst komplexe technische Zusammenhänge für alle verständlich. Durch das frühzeitige Erkennen und proaktive Minimieren technischer und projektbezogener Risiken stellst du reibungslose Entwicklungsprozesse über alle Phasen hinweg sicher. Du schreibst Clean Code für nachhaltige, hochgradig zuverlässige Software und teilst dein Wissen aktiv im Team, beispielsweise im Rahmen von Code-Reviews. Dein Rucksack für diese Stelle Du bringst über 5 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung als Softwareentwickler:in mit TypeScript mit – sowohl im Frontend als auch im Backend. Du entwickelst performante Single-Page-Applications mit Vue.js und sauberer API-Anbindung an Node.js-Backends. Du verfügst über fundierte Erfahrung in der Backend-Entwicklung mit Node.js, idealerweise mit NestJS, sowie im Design von REST-APIs inklusive OAuth 2.0. Nachweisbare Kompetenz in der Entwicklung und strategischen Entscheidungsfindung für anspruchsvolle Softwarearchitekturen, dem Schreiben von Clean Code sowie der Umsetzung von Frontend- und Backend-Tests zeichnet dich aus. Du bringst umfassende Praxiserfahrung mit relationalen Datenbanken (PostgreSQL) sowie der asynchronen Verarbeitung über Task Queues oder Messaging-Systeme mit. Du hast ein ausgeprägtes Verständnis für Web-Application-Security, wie etwa die OWASP Top 10, sichere Authentifizierung und Autorisierung sowie den Schutz sensibler Finanz- und Personendaten. Help build fair, engaged and high-performing teams.
We believe everyone deserves a fair opportunity to develop and be rewarded for the value they bring. That's why we build software that helps organizations set clear expectations, define what a role entails, assess performance fairly, support employee growth and make compensation transparent and explainable. From clear roles to fair rewards, all within one continuous process. 

We do this with a driven team of 55+ colleagues. Hundreds of companies in the Netherlands, from scale-ups to corporates, already use Learned. Now we're taking the next step: Germany. 

As Senior Partnership Manager Germany you're part of our founding DE team. You build the partner channel from scratch and become the face of Learned in the German HR ecosystem.

Lay the foundation for our partner channel in Germany

You build our German partner channel from the ground up. You decide how we do partnerships in Germany, and then you make it happen: from the first partner to a network that brings in a steady flow of new business.

Our network has two parts:

  • Implementation partners: HR consultants and advisory firms that bring Learned to their clients.

  • Learning partners: companies specialized in job evaluation and learning & development.

What you’ll do

  • Set the strategy. Map the German HR ecosystem and decide which partners to focus on first. Set clear targets for the channel and make sure partners and direct sales strengthen each other.

  • Build the foundation. Shape the partner model for Germany: partner tiers, the commercial terms, and the playbook and processes that let the channel grow. Our Dutch partner programme is your starting point. You adapt it to the German market.

  • Find and close new partners. Start conversations at board level, then negotiate and close partnerships.

  • Turn partners into growth. Onboard and enable partners, build joint plans and turn them into a steady source of new business.

  • Activate the market. Put Learned on the map in Germany with partner and customer events, such as roundtables, webinars and breakfast sessions. You work together with marketing and get operational support for running them.

How your time is split (at the start)

  • ~50%: Finding new partners

  • ~30%: Partner management

  • ~10%: Events and activation

  • ~10%: Strategy

As the network grows, your focus shifts towards partner management and scaling the channel. You might also build a team around it.

Who you work with

You report to our Partnership Lead in NL and work closely with our Founding Account Executive Germany..

Where you'll work

You choose one of two setups:

  • Based in or around Düsseldorf or Cologne. You work remotely in North Rhine-Westphalia, close to your partners and visit our office in Utrecht regularly. We plan to open an office in Düsseldorf or Cologne, and you'll help build it.

  • Based in or around Utrecht (NL). You work from our office in Utrecht and travel to the NRW region about twice a month for a few days.

Either way, you start with an onboarding at our office in Utrecht.


Who you are

  • A bachelor's or master's level of thinking and working

  • At least 8 years of experience in business development, partnerships, sales or account management, ideally in SaaS or HR tech

  • A track record of building partner channels or new markets from scratch

  • An existing network in the German HR, consulting or HR-tech ecosystem is a big plus

  • Native German speaker and fluent in English. Dutch is a plus.

  • You're an entrepreneurial hunter: you open doors, talk easily at board level and close deals on your own

  • You're organised, think strategically and keep the overview while doing the hands-on work

  • You have an affinity with HR, learning & development or technology

What we offer

We're ambitious and entrepreneurial, and we take steps towards our big goals together every day. Having fun matters just as much. You get:

  • €70,000 – €80,000 base salary and €90,000 – €100,000 OTE gross per year

  • A rare chance to be part of our founding team in Germany and shape the market from day one

  • A local employment contract in Germany through our employer of record partner (or a Dutch contract if you're based in the Netherlands)

  • A MacBook and everything you need to do your job well

  • 25 vacation days (full-time)

  • Travel allowance and travel costs for your trips to Germany or the Netherlands

  • A personal development budget of €1,000 per year

  • An ambitious, international team with 7+ nationalities, where we keep each other sharp and celebrate successes

  • When you're in Utrecht: a daily (healthy) lunch with the team and a fun team activity every month

Excited to learn more about this opportunity and whether there’s a potential match? There's only one way to find out. Apply now as Senior Partnership Manager Germany!

title: Defense Success Manager, France
description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes. Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support. This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job. You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them): Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing. Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals. In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout. What You Will Do Own the customer success and value plan Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes. Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear. Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative. Make deployment realities part of the success plan Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models. Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders. Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited. Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments. Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks. Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement. Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently. raw.title: Defense Success Manager, France
raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes.

Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

  • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

  • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.


What You Will Do


Own the customer success and value plan

  • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

  • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

  • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

  • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

  • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

  • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

  • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

  • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

  • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

  • Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

  • Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

  • Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

  • Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

  • Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner.

  • Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

  • Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

  • Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience owning outcomes for enterprise or institutional customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting.

  • Strong technical fluency in secure enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premise, disconnected, air-gapped) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and accreditation, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity.

  • Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security stakeholders, while translating technical trade-offs into clear implications for mission owners and executives. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert.

  • Comfort operating under security, compliance and confidentiality constraints, including restricted or classified environments and strict information-handling rules.

  • Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion

  • Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics with imperfect data, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability.


Nice to have

  • Experience serving defense, public sector or critical infrastructure customers, including sovereign or classified programs.

  • Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments.

  • Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation.

  • Familiarity with public procurement, framework agreements and multi-year option structures.

Security & Compliance criteria

  • Eligibility: must hold citizenship in the target territory (France for now).

  • Clearable: must meet all local requirements for high-level security clearance (e.g. no criminal record, fulfillment of national service obligations).

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.
